sessions.title: App boots and shows data
sessions.goal: Boot the app, serve the seeded expenses via an API, render an expenses table, and show per-person totals-paid.

criteria.check: GET /api/expenses returns 200 with a JSON array of 4 Expense
sc-home renders 4 elements with data-testid=expense-row after load
sc-home shows a per-person totals-paid summary with 5 rows and exact amounts: Alice $52.00, Bob $30.00, Cara $40.00, Dan $15.00, Eve $0.00

cuts.hint: Put every expense from the seed store into `body` and set `status` to 200
Fetch "/api/expenses" and write the parsed JSON array into `items`; keep the existing error and loading state handling unchanged
Accumulate the sum of `amountCents` each payer contributed into `totals` keyed by person id using integer cents already present in `items`

sessions.title: Netting works and a naive settlement renders
sessions.goal: Compute per-person net balances (paid minus owed) and show a naive greedy settlement on the page; expose the same transfers via an API.
teaches: pure functions over arrays and maps
wiring computed data into UI and an endpoint

criteria.check: sc-home renders 5 elements with data-testid=balance-row in name-ASC order, with exact texts: Alice +$26.00; Bob -$6.00; Cara +$4.00; Dan -$11.00; Eve -$13.00
sc-home renders a Proposed transfers list with 4 elements with data-testid=transfer-row and the first item reads "Eve pays Alice $13.00"
sc-home shows a total transfers amount element [data-testid=transfers-total] equal to "$30.00"
GET /api/settlement/naive returns 200 with a JSON array of 4 Transfer; the first element equals {"from":"Eve","to":"Alice","amountCents":1300}

cuts.hint: Compute each person's net in cents into `out` by adding amounts they paid and subtracting their share of each expense; divide an expense by the sum of participant weights (default 1) and subtract each share from that participant

From a `balances` map, build `out` as a list of transfers by repeatedly matching the largest positive balance to the largest (most negative) balance and moving the smaller absolute amount; continue until no balances remain nonzero
Derive `balances` from the loaded `items` (and the current included people) using the provided netting function
Derive `transfers` from the current `balances` using the naive settlement function and make it stable across renders
Populate `body` with the current naive settlement computed from the seeded expenses and set `status` to 200

sessions.title: Minimal-mode, integer formatting, and include/exclude
sessions.goal: Add a minimal-mode toggle that switches to a refined, deterministically ordered settlement for display; format all money with integer-safe cents; and add include/exclude per person that immediately recomputes balances and transfers.
teaches: local UI toggles that drive recomputation

criteria.check: With [data-testid=toggle-minimal] set ON, sc-home renders the transfers in amount-descending order then payer then payee; the sequence reads exactly: "Eve pays Alice $13.00", "Dan pays Alice $11.00", "Bob pays Cara $4.00", "Bob pays Alice $2.00"
Unchecking [data-testid=include-Eve] removes Eve from balances and no [data-testid=transfer-row] contains "Eve"
With [data-testid=toggle-minimal] set ON, sc-home renders 4 elements with data-testid=transfer-row
With [data-testid=toggle-minimal] set OFF, sc-home renders the last [data-testid=transfer-row] item as "Bob pays Cara $4.00"

cuts.hint: Format integer cents into `out` as "$X.YY" with a leading minus for negatives (e.g. -615 → "-$6.15"); do not use floats
Produce `out` as a transfer list equivalent in totals to the naive result but ordered by amount descending, then payer asc, then payee asc; do not increase the number of transfers
Toggle the given person's id in the `included` Set while preserving every other selection; the next recompute must use exactly the currently included people
When minimal mode is ON, write the refined transfer sequence into `transfers` using the minimal function; when it is OFF, preserve the naive sequence already derived
